
# Welcome to PSYCH 420!

## Overview

::: {.card-list .nonincremental}
- Lab logistics
- Teaching philosophy
- Checking R installation
:::

## How does this course work?
::: {.card-list}
- Hybrid format
- There are online "content modules" and in-person labs
- The topics will be related, but I do not know much about what is going on in the online modules
- So if you have any questions about the online modules, email Alex, or go to his office hours.
- I highly recommend going to his office hours. He's super nice!

:::


## Lab logistics

::: card-list
- In this lab section, you will learn how to 1) code in R and 2) do statistics in R.
- Each week you will submit a lab report by the end of class.
- I grade these labs on the spot in the lab, so you can make sure you get a full score before you submit them
- You will also complete 4 case studies this semester. These are extended versions of lab reports where you will be asked to apply what you learned to analyze a novel dataset. 
- Detailed rubrics will be posted on the lab website
- A more detailed syllubus can be found on Canvas

:::

## Lab website
::: card-list
- We have a separate website for the lab. 
- Please use the lab website, and not Canvas, to download lab related materials and case study rubrics.
- The lab slides will also be posted on the website.
- However, assignments should be submitted through Canvas
- <https://monaxue.github.io/420m/>

:::


## Teaching philosophy

::: card-list

- My primary goals is to help you learn
- I believe that every single one of you can can succeed in this class
- That being said, this class will not be easy
- The most successful students in my class are those that
    - Actively participated in class
    - Asked for a lot of help

:::

## Communication is key

::: card-list

- Don't be afraid to reach out to me. If you have questions or are struggling with assignments, please please reach out!
- I try to be an understanding person, but can only do so if you communicate with me. Please reach out to me if you have any concerns about your abilities to attend class, complete assignments, etc. 


:::

## Teaching philosophy

::: card-list
- I believe that the best way to learn involves 1) solving problems on your own, 2) discussing problems with peers, 3) asking for help.
- Therefore, I have structured the lab section so you can
    - Code independenty, instead of just copying what I do
    - Discuss questions with your peers
    - Get direct feedback from me on your deliverables
- Because of the way I structure class, class usually takes up the full two hours.

:::

## Teaching philosophy

::: card-list

- Again, I want to emphasize in class participation

- I will be using polls for attendance, but you are also expected to participate

:::

## AI usage

::: card-list

- Like with any other sources, I see AI as tool that can help you learn
- So I allow AI only in as much that you actually understand what you are doing
- If you use any external sources for your case studies, you must explain where and how you used it
- Those who rely on AI to generate their lab reports and case studies do not get good grades
    - AI generated reports are just not that good
    - It is clear to me when there is lack of understanding in the report

:::

## R installation and setup

::: {.card-list .nonincremental}

1. Install both R and R RStudio: https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/
1. In the console of RStudio, run these
    - `install.packages("tidyverse")`
    - `install.packages("ggplot2")`
1. Run the RMarkdown file, `test.Rmd`, to see if it's working. 
    1. Go to <https://monaxue.github.io/420m/>. and download `test.Rmd`. Then open it in Rstudio.
    1. Click on the "Knit" button
![](/assets/Screenshot 2026-01-15 210009.png)
1. When your RMarkdown file has successfully generated a `.html` file, let me know, and I will come check that it was successful. After you have shown me your file, you are free to leave.

:::
